```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE)
```

This is a concrete, step-by-step walkthrough of the most common
maintenance task on a live Promotion Review Tracker install: adding
one new field to a form that already has data in it. It uses a real
example -- adding a `review_assigned_date` field to the
`journal_reviews` form -- with the exact commands that were run
against a live deployment while writing this guide.

This is a worked instance of the general procedure in
`vignette('promotion-tracker-technical-guide')`, Section 10
("Updating the Data Dictionary After Go-Live"). Read that section
first if you have not already; this document does not repeat its
warnings, only applies them.

**A word on "rebuilding" the database.** If your instinct is to
re-run `setup_zzedc_from_gsheets()` to pick up a Data Dictionary
change, stop. That function calls
`initialize_encrypted_database()` internally, and with
`overwrite = TRUE` it deletes the existing database file and
creates an empty one with a brand-new encryption key and salt --
every record anyone has entered is gone, with no recovery path.
There is no supported "rebuild in place" operation. What this guide
does instead is add the one new column to the running database
directly, which takes under a second and touches nothing else.

---

## For a non-technical trial manager: what you can do yourself

If you are a trial manager without database access, you can still do
the recordkeeping half of this change yourself in the Google Sheet --
you just cannot finish it alone.

**What you can do in Google Sheets.** Open the Promotion Review
Tracker Sheet, go to the `Data_Dictionary` tab, find the rows for
`journal_reviews`, and add one new row:

| Column | Value |
|---|---|
| form_code | journal_reviews |
| field_name | review_assigned_date |
| field_label | Review Assigned Date |
| field_type | date |
| required | FALSE |
| description | Date the editor assigned this manuscript for review |
| field_order | 35 |

Use `field_order = 35` so the new field lands between Manuscript ID
(30) and Review Date (40) -- the gaps of 10 between existing rows
exist exactly so a new row can be slotted in without renumbering
anything else.

**Where it stops being a Sheet-only job.** Editing the Sheet does
*not*, by itself, make the field appear in the live app. There is no
automatic sync from the Sheet to the running form -- the Sheet is the
durable record of what the form *should* contain, but someone with
database access still has to apply the matching change to the live
database (Sections 2-3 below). That step takes an admin under a
minute. In practice: update the Sheet for recordkeeping and audit
purposes, then hand off to whoever manages the deployment to apply it
live.

---

## 1. Update the Google Sheet first

The Google Sheet's `Data_Dictionary` tab is the durable source of
truth: it is what a fresh install or a disaster-recovery rebuild
reads from, so an addition that only exists in the live database and
not in the Sheet will be silently lost the next time someone
provisions a new copy of this study from scratch. Always update the
Sheet, even though (as of this writing) there is no supported
re-import path that would pick the change up automatically on a live
database -- Section 2 below is still a separate step.

Open the Sheet (Section 6.1 of the technical guide has the URL and
tab-naming rules) and add one row to `Data_Dictionary`:

| form_code | field_name | field_label | field_type | required | validation | description | field_order | widget | help_detail |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| journal_reviews | review_assigned_date | Review Assigned Date | date | FALSE | | Date the editor assigned this manuscript for review | 35 | | |

Two things about this row that are easy to get wrong:

- **`field_order` controls display position, not just sort order
  within the sheet.** The existing `journal_reviews` rows are
  ordered 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60 (`tracking_id` through `notes`).
  Picking `35` places the new field between `manuscript_id` (30) and
  `review_date` (40) -- logically correct, since a review is
  assigned before it is completed. Leaving gaps of 10 between
  existing rows is exactly so a later insertion like this one does
  not require renumbering anything else.
- **`field_type` in the Sheet is lower case** (`date`), matching
  every other row. The importer upper-cases it internally before
  storing it. This matters in Section 2 below, where
  `add_form_field_by_code()` requires the upper-case form
  explicitly.

If you maintain a local mirror of the Data Dictionary (this
package's own demonstration study keeps one at
`vignettes/promotion-tracker/Data_Dictionary.csv`), update it the
same way and keep the two in sync:

```{r}
dd <- read.csv('Data_Dictionary.csv', stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

new_row <- dd[1, ]
new_row[1, ]         <- NA
new_row$form_code    <- 'journal_reviews'
new_row$field_name   <- 'review_assigned_date'
new_row$field_label  <- 'Review Assigned Date'
new_row$field_type   <- 'date'
new_row$required     <- FALSE
new_row$validation   <- ''
new_row$description  <- 'Date the editor assigned this manuscript for review'
new_row$field_order  <- 35
new_row$widget       <- ''
new_row$help_detail  <- ''

dd2 <- rbind(dd, new_row)
dd2 <- dd2[order(dd2$form_code, dd2$field_order), ]
write.csv(dd2, 'Data_Dictionary.csv', row.names = FALSE)
```

Push the updated data frame to the Sheet with `sheet_write()`
(Section 6.1), or edit the row directly in the Sheets UI -- either
is fine, as long as the two end up identical.

```{r}
library(googlesheets4)
gs4_auth(email = 'you@example.com')

sheet_write(dd2, ss = 'YOUR_SHEET_ID', sheet = 'Data_Dictionary')
```

---

## 2. Add the field to the live database

### The normal path: `add_form_field_by_code()`

With `DB_ENCRYPTION_KEY` and `ZZEDC_SALT` exported for this session
(Section 8 of the technical guide), `add_form_field_by_code()` does
the rest of this section in one call: it resolves `form_code` to the
form's `design_id`, checks for a duplicate `field_code` on that form,
inserts the field, and reads the row back to confirm it was written
exactly as requested. **`field_type` must still be the upper-case
constant**, from `get_designer_field_types()` -- `"DATE"`, not
`"date"`. Passing the lower-case Sheet spelling fails with `Invalid
field_type: date`; the Google Sheets importer upper-cases it for you
on the way in, but this direct call does not.

```{r}
library(zzedc)

result <- add_form_field_by_code(
  form_code    = 'journal_reviews',       # matched case-insensitively
  field_code   = 'review_assigned_date',
  field_label  = 'Review Assigned Date',
  field_type   = 'DATE',
  field_row    = 35,                      # matches field_order above
  field_column = 1,
  is_required  = FALSE,
  help_text    = 'Date the editor assigned this manuscript for review'
)
result$success    # TRUE if the field was added
result$verified    # TRUE if the row read back matches every argument
result$design_id   # resolved from form_code -- no manual lookup needed
```

`field_row` here plays the same role as `field_order` in the
Data Dictionary: it is the field's position among its form's other
fields, not a literal UI grid row. Giving it the same value you put
in the Sheet keeps the two in agreement, which matters if you ever
import a fresh copy of this study and compare the two field lists.

Re-running this block by accident is safe: `add_form_field_by_code()`
checks for a `field_code` already on that `design_id` before
inserting, and returns `result$success == FALSE` with
`result$error` naming the existing `field_id` rather than creating a
second copy.

```{r}
result$success    # FALSE on a repeat call
result$error       # "Field 'review_assigned_date' already exists on ..."
result$field_id    # the id of the field that already exists
```

An unrecognized `form_code` fails the same way, before anything is
written: `result$success == FALSE` with `result$error` reading `"No
form found with form_code: ..."`.

### If it fails with "Database encryption key not found"

`add_form_field_by_code()` connects through `connect_encrypted_db()`
(the same path `add_form_field()` uses), which hard-stops if
`DB_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is not set in the current R session -- by
design, so a stray script can never silently touch an encrypted
database it has no business opening. Re-export the key (Section 8)
and retry.

If your deployment is one where the database's "encryption" is
known not to be doing anything (flagged in
`vignette('zzedc-whitepaper')` as an open finding, not a supported
mode of operation -- track the real fix there, do not treat the
workaround below as a substitute for it), a direct `RSQLite`
connection reaches the same file without the key check, and you can
insert the row by hand with the identical shape
`add_form_field_by_code()` would have written. This requires the
form's `design_id`, which the escape hatch has no way to resolve for
you (that lookup is the part of `add_form_field_by_code()` that
needs the key-checked connection):

```{r}
conn <- DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), 'data/zzedc.db')

design_id <- DBI::dbGetQuery(conn,
  "SELECT design_id FROM designer_forms WHERE UPPER(form_code) = 'JOURNAL_REVIEWS'"
)$design_id[1]

existing <- DBI::dbGetQuery(conn, "
  SELECT field_id FROM designer_fields
  WHERE design_id = ? AND field_code = 'review_assigned_date'
", params = list(design_id))

if (nrow(existing) == 0) {
  DBI::dbExecute(conn, "
    INSERT INTO designer_fields
      (design_id, field_code, field_label, field_type, field_row,
       field_column, field_width, is_required, is_visible, help_text)
    VALUES
      (?, 'review_assigned_date', 'Review Assigned Date', 'DATE', 35, 1,
       100, 0, 1, 'Date the editor assigned this manuscript for review')
  ", params = list(design_id))
}

DBI::dbDisconnect(conn)
```

Treat this as an admin-only escape hatch, not routine practice: it
bypasses the package's own validation (`is_backend_available`,
field-type checking) and the key-gated connection that
`add_form_field_by_code()` enforces. Prefer the normal path above
whenever the encryption key is actually available to you.

**Neither path writes to the audit trail.** Despite the parallel to
other mutating operations in this package, `add_form_field()` and
`add_form_field_by_code()` do not call `log_audit_event()` --
confirmed by inspection, `R/crf_designer.R` has no reference to it
at all, unlike `R/adverse_events.R`, `R/data_correction.R`,
`R/version_control.R`, and the other modules that do. Adding or
editing a field through either path leaves no row in `audit_log`;
the only record of the change is whatever the Google Sheet and this
walkthrough's own command history capture. This is a real gap, not
a design choice documented elsewhere, and is tracked in
`vignette('zzedc-whitepaper')`.

---

## 3. Verify

`result$verified` from Section 2 already confirms the database side:
it is `TRUE` only when the row read back from `designer_fields`
matches every argument passed in (label, type, position, required
flag, help text), and `result$mismatches` names exactly which ones
did not match on the rare occasion it is `FALSE`. That rules the
database out as a cause if the field still does not show up live --
at that point the cause is the running browser tab, not the data, so
the one thing left to check by hand is the UI rendering itself.

No application restart and no package reinstall are needed. Unlike
an R code change (which requires `R CMD INSTALL` and a fresh R
session, per Section 12's note on `library()` being a no-op when the
package is already attached), a `designer_fields` row is read fresh
from the database on every page load -- the dynamic form renderer
queries it live.

Reload the EDC tab in the browser, switch the **Form** selector to
**JOURNAL_REVIEWS Form**, and confirm:

- **Review Assigned Date** appears as a date field, positioned
  between Manuscript ID and Review Date.
- It has no red required-asterisk (it was added with
  `is_required = FALSE`).
- Clicking its hint icon shows the help text: "Date the editor
  assigned this manuscript for review."

If the field does not appear, the most likely cause is a stale
reactive cache in an already-open browser tab rather than anything
wrong with the database row -- a hard reload (not just re-clicking
the form tab) forces the metadata query to re-run.

---

## 4. What this walkthrough deliberately did not do

- **No validation rule was added** (e.g. requiring
  `review_date >= review_assigned_date`). Nothing in the original
  request called for one; see
  `vignette('content-author-guide')` for the DSL syntax if you want
  to add one later, following the pattern of
  `MENTOR_END_AFTER_START` / `COMM_END_AFTER_START` in the technical
  guide's validation-rules table (Section 6.1).
- **The field was not marked required.** Existing `journal_reviews`
  records have no value for it and would fail validation retroactively
  if it were.
- **No backup was taken before this change.** Adding a column is
  additive and reversible (`DROP COLUMN` or simply ignoring the new
  field in the UI), unlike the destructive `overwrite = TRUE`
  rebuild this guide opened by warning against -- but Section 9 of
  the technical guide's backup routine costs little and is worth
  running on a schedule regardless.
